transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door interlock / monitor microswitch (electrical start path). With it unplugged, look at the plastic hooks on the edge of the door and the slots they click into, and check the door shuts cleanly — food or grease in the slots can stop them engaging. Was there food / grease in the way (and is it cleaned), is a hook or latch broken, or does it all look fine?

There was some grease around the door hooks and latch slots. I cleaned it, but it has still happened once since. No broken hooks that I can see. The door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, though I can't be sure. No burning smell, sparks or tripping either.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door alignment / hinge / accessible obstruction. Plug it back in and try a cup of water for a minute. Does the door latch and the microwave start normally now, or still not?

I can't really test it the way you describe, as the fault is intermittent. It heats normally most of the time and only cuts out every few days, more often when I close the door gently. I can't take it out of the housing either as it's screwed into the tall unit. What do you suggest?

This behavior strongly suggests a failing door interlock switch or latch mechanism, as the appliance resumes only when the door is physically manipulated. You should replace the door latch assembly and associated switches to resolve this intermittent safety cut-out. Next: Do not force or pry the door open. Let me know what you find.

I can't get at the switches without taking the unit out of the housing, and I won't do that. Is this something I should get an engineer in for? It's about 4 years old, so out of Bosch's 2-year warranty, but I'd pay for a visit.

Unplug it first and never remove the outer casing. Yes, you should get an engineer in because the intermittent fault and misaligned door suggest a mechanical or safety switch issue that requires professional diagnosis. Attempting to repair microwave high-voltage components yourself is unsafe and not recommended. Next: Do not remove the microwave casing. Let me know what you find.
